subject: Capacity fit analysis and conservative headroom for VerdentX commit
messages:
From: Alex Grover <alex.grover@verdentx.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Menon <p.menon@verdentx.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — VerdentX expected traffic profile attached

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, VerdentX is trying to finalize the committing slab for our pilot-to-prod ramp and we need a Redwood recommendation for Dedicated capacity (GPU slab + burst policy) that meets our p95 response SLO.

Quick context:
- Model: customer-finetuned rw-gpt-13b-quant (serving variants: 1-shot prompt + generation)
- Typical generation length: 60–100 tokens (median ~80)
- Expected production peak: ~120 requests/sec sustained during business peaks (short bursts to ~200 req/sec)
- Traffic profile attached: verdentx_traffic_profile.csv (hourly samples, concurrency distribution)
- Target SLO: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 250ms (for 80-token median)
- Compliance: data residency + VPC (we'll take Redwood Private later), initial ask is Dedicated reserved slab for US region

Can you provide an initial tokens/sec translate and a conservative slab recommendation (including headroom and fallback policy) — we need this for procurement & procurement sign-off next week.

Appreciate it,
Alex

--
Alex Grover
Head of Platform, VerdentX
alex.grover@verdentx.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Grover <alex.grover@verdentx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — VerdentX expected traffic profile attached

Hi Alex — thanks for the profile, this is exactly what we need. I ran a quick translation from requests/sec to tokens/sec and attached a rough capacity workbook (vdx_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with the math. High level below.

Summary (baseline -> conservative):
- Baseline peak traffic: 120 req/s * 80 tokens/req = 9,600 tokens/sec sustained
- Burst peak observed in file: up to ~200 req/s -> 200 * 80 = 16,000 tokens/sec instantaneous
- Measured throughput for your model (rw-gpt-13b-quant) on our bench (A100 80GB, optimized kernels, 512-context) ~= 3,000 tokens/sec per GPU when sustaining generation with continuous batching enabled

Raw GPUs required (no headroom):
- Sustained baseline: ceil(9,600 / 3,000) = 4 GPUs
- Burst instantaneous: ceil(16,000 / 3,000) = 6 GPUs

Conservative planning guidance (what we recommend for a committed slab):
- Committed slab: 6 GPUs reserved (this covers expected bursts but leaves little ops buffer)
- Preferred committed slab: 8 GPUs reserved — gives ~1.6x headroom on sustained baseline and ~1.5x on observed bursts after scheduling/variance; this aligns with our typical safety factor for new customers during the 0–6 month ramp
- Autoscale/burst policy: allow bursts up to +4 GPUs (on top of the committed slab) for short windows (minutes) using our Dedicated burst pool — ensures we can absorb traffic spikes to ~20k tokens/sec without immediate throttling

SLO mapping (p95):
- At 3k t/s per GPU, an 80-token generation is roughly 27ms pure token-streaming time; with batching, KV/cache warmups, and network overhead we estimate end-to-end p95 ~140–200ms per request on the committed slab (8 GPUs) under typical load — within your 250ms target

Next steps: Ben (cc'd) will scope the formal capacity workbook and include a latency sensitivity curve (p50/p95/p99) and a runbook for warmup + cache seeding. I'll also flag procurement templates.

Attached: vdx_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (workbook), I used your verdentx_traffic_profile.csv as input.

Do you want us to present this math to VerdentX procurement and security next Thursday?

Thanks,
Stephanie
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Grover <alex.grover@verdentx.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Jun 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — VerdentX expected traffic profile attached

Alex / team — expanding on Stephanie's quick calc with the operational guardrails and a slightly more conservative engineering view. I pasted the key rows from the workbook below for visibility.

Key assumptions in the workbook:
- Model variant: rw-gpt-13b-quant, 512 context, continuous batching with target batch window 20ms
- Per-GPU sustained measured throughput (A100 80GB): 3,000 tokens/sec (median across repeats). We use 2,800 t/s as an engineering safety number to allow for queueing overheads & variable prompt lengths.
- Cold-start/warmup: first few requests may hit KV cache misses — plan for a short warmup period and pre-warm critical routes via cache seeding at deploy time

Detailed numbers (rounded):
- Baseline sustained tokens/sec: 9,600 -> GPUs @ 2,800 t/s = ceil(9,600/2,800) = 4 GPUs (sustained)
- Operationally safe sustained: add 40% headroom -> 4 * 1.4 = 5.6 -> round up -> 6 GPUs
- Burst capacity (200 req/s -> 16,000 t/s): GPUs @ 2,800 = ceil(16,000/2,800) = 6 GPUs; with 40% safety -> 9 GPUs

Recommendation (ops + procurement):
- Committed slab: 6 GPUs (minimum for sustained plus a small safety buffer)
- Launcher slab (what we provision for go-live): 8 GPUs reserved for month 1–3 to absorb early pattern variance while we calibrate batching and caching
- Burst pool: enable autoscale to add up to +4 GPUs for short bursts (this takes you to 12 GPUs available quickly)
- Maintenance & redundancy: plan for 1 GPU spare during rolling maintenance (i.e., keep one GPU headroom so live capacity doesn't dip below committed)

SLO sensitivity:
- With the 8-GPU launcher slab and aggressive batching we project p95 E2E = 160–210ms for 80-token median; p99 tail edges toward 280–340ms under pathological bursts (hence the burst pool recommendation)

Cost implications and deal structuring:
- We can price the committed 6–8 GPU slab as a Tier-2 Dedicated commitment; adding the burst pool is an add-on priced by peak usage and minutes used.
- If VerdentX wants to reduce committed spend, we can structure a commit-to-burst credit model (commit to 6 GPUs, with monthly overage credits applied when burst pool used) — I can draft a term sheet after procurement confirms target spend range.

Operational notes (runbook items):
- Pre-warm tooling: pre-seed common prompts and maintain a KV cache TTL aligned to request patterns (we'll advise specific keys).
- Canary + rollback: use 10% traffic canary on day-1 after deployment to validate p95; auto-fallback to quantized smaller variant if regressions detected.
- Observable signals: token/sec, qps, p95 latency by route, kernel stalls, GPU utilization. Thresholds in the workbook link.

If that looks good we'll prepare a one-page capacity summary for procurement and a drive folder with the workbook + perf traces.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
